image_description: Two men in outdoor fishing gear (red rain suit and green jacket) are holding a large, grey fish horizontally. The background shows a body of water and distant hills under an overcast sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish displays the characteristic elongated snout and the mouth is clearly positioned on the underside (ventral) of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Four distinct, fleshy barbel structures are visible hanging down from the snout area in front of the mouth.
The anterior part of the head tapers to a distinct point, consistent with sturgeon morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish has a long, torpedo-shaped (fusiform) body that spans the width held by the two men, indicating significant length.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Prominent, raised bony plates (scutes) are clearly visible running longitudinally along the lateral line and dorsal ridge; typical fish scales are absent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the fish is dark grey/brown, transitioning to a white/lighter color on the belly, matching the expected countershading.
Although partially obscured by the man's hand, the visible portion of the caudal fin shows the upper lobe extending further than the lower lobe, characteristic of a heterocercal tail.
